Anita (PM): Heads up — two field customers asked about forced upgrades for private deploys this week. They want an automatic push to keep them on latest security patches. Can eng + netops weigh in on feasibility, rollback safety, and customer-managed networking impacts?

Devin (Eng): Quick q — do they mean automatic without confirmation (zero-touch), or an opt-in scheduled window? big difference for operator design. :thinking:

Anita (PM): Zero-touch would be ideal for them, but one asked specifically for a scheduled maintenance window (nightly). Another explicitly said they don't want any change without approval. mixed asks.

Jared (NetOps): We need to preserve customer egress IPs and NAT mappings. Forced operator upgrades that restart pods could change ephemeral IPs if they're using nodePort/hostNetwork. That will break static firewall rules on customer side.

Lina (SRE): Also worry about KV cache and model warmup. A mass restart across tenants causes immediate 99th pct latency blips. We should avoid simultaneous restarts.

Devin (Eng): From runtime side, we can support rolling upgrades by tenant/operator shard with backoff. Two options: in-place operator upgrade (keep host networking) or forklift (new nodes + cordon/evict). Both need a graceful drain strategy.

Jared (NetOps): Forklift helps keep stable egress IPs if we provision nodes behind the same NAT, but some customers run strict IP pinning and expect zero-new-connections drop. We'll need an egress-preservation contract and docs.

Anita (PM): For launch criteria I propose: (1) documented rollback playbook, (2) ability to schedule upgrades per-customer timezone, (3) egress IP preservation guidance + test checklist, (4) canary rollout to 5% of tenants with metric gating. Thoughts?

Devin (Eng): +1. For rollback we need image pinning and a one-command revert that reprovisions previous operator + model bundle. Suggest we add an automated smoke test that runs post-upgrade and triggers rollback on failure.

Lina (SRE): Smoke tests should include: token latency < 200ms p50 on a sample prompt, KV cache hit rates, and inference error rate < 0.5%. If any fail, automatic rollback to previous image. Include circuit-breaker for rate spikes.

Jared (NetOps): Add network tests: TCP handshake to customer IPs, validate egress IP via curl to an echo endpoint, verify BGP session stays established (for customers using BGP).

upgrade-bot: Deploy plan created: upgrade/1745127890/plan (internal only) :robot_face:

Anita (PM): Ok action items: Devin drafts rollback playbook + one-click revert command by EOD next Tue; Jared drafts egress preservation checklist and test harness; Lina publishes smoke-test criteria. We'll gate GA on successful 3-customer canary across distinct network topologies.

Devin (Eng): Will sketch the operator flow. tentative CLI snippet for revert: ```sh
# revert operator to previous tag
kubectl apply -f operator-v1.2.3.yaml
# wait for pods ready
./scripts/check-smoke.sh || ./scripts/rollback.sh
```

Jared (NetOps): I'll mock the IP-preserve test: ```sh
# validate egress IP
curl -s https://echo-ip.example.com && echo "ok"
# validate BGP (if present)
ssh netbox@customer-bgp 'show bgp summary'
```

Lina (SRE): I'll author the smoke check harness and add threshold alerts in Console. Need someone to own runbook readout for field eng — Anita?

Anita (PM): I'll run the readout and coordinate customer acceptance testing. Thanks all — marking this thread for the next PrivDeploy sync. :thumbsup:

Devin (Eng): one more Q — do we permit forced upgrades for air-gapped installs? that raises signing/transport constraints.

Jared (NetOps): For airgap, we only supply signed bundles and an offline apply path. Forced push is impossible; must be customer-initiated. Call that out in the playbook.

Anita (PM): noted. I'll include that as a hard constraint. Closing with owners: Devin (rollback playbook), Jared (egress tests), Lina (smoke harness), Anita (customer readout).
